g1.label: 1. ___ works at a hospital
g1.why: The subject of the sentence is Ana, a woman. A subject pronoun for one woman is "she", not the object form "her".

g2.label: 2. ___ studies music
g2.why: The subject is Tom, a man, so use "he". "Him" is for objects and "his" shows ownership.

g3.label: 3. bought ___ a blue scarf
g3.why: The grandmother receives the scarf, so she is the object of "bought". Use the object pronoun "her", not "she".

g4.label: 4. ___ gave it to her
g4.why: Ana and Tom together are the subject of the sentence, so use "They". "Them" is only for objects.

g5.label: 5. she loved ___
g5.why: The scarf is the object of "loved", and one thing is "it". "Them" would mean more than one thing.

g6.label: 6. Tom took ___ photo
g6.why: Spaced review from the Articles exercise: the photo is mentioned for the first time, so use "a".

g1.label: 1. My sister and ___ share a room.
g1.why: "I" is a subject pronoun. In a pair like "My sister and I", check by removing the other person: "I share a room".

g2.label: 2. The teacher likes Mia. She often helps ___ with her homework.
g2.why: "Helps" needs an object after it, and Mia is one woman. Use the object pronoun "her", not "she".

g3.label: 3. ___ are late for the bus again.
g3.why: The pronoun is the subject of "are", so use "We". "Us" is the object form.

g4.label: 4. Sam and I need help. Can you help ___?
g4.why: "Help" needs an object. "Us" means Sam and me, as the object of "help".

g5.label: 5. My parents are strict, but I love ___ very much.
g5.why: "Love" needs an object, and "my parents" is plural. The object pronoun for more than one person is "them".

g6.label: 6. Where is Ben? I can't find ___ anywhere.
g6.why: "Find" needs an object, and Ben is a man. The object pronoun is "him", not "he".

g7.label: 7. Dan and Eva are friends. ___ play tennis together.
g7.why: Dan and Eva are the subject of "play", so use the subject pronoun "They".

g8.label: 8. Between you and ___, the film was boring.
g8.why: After a preposition such as "between" use the object form: "between you and me", not "between you and I".

g1.label: 1. This isn't my pen. ___ is on the desk.
g1.why: No noun follows the gap, so we need a possessive pronoun. "Mine" means "my pen". "My" always needs a noun after it.

g2.label: 2. I cut ___ while I was cooking.
g2.why: The person who cuts and the person who is cut are the same, so use the reflexive pronoun "myself".

g3.label: 3. Is this your bag? No, the red one is ___.
g3.why: "The red one" is the thing, so no noun follows the gap. Use the possessive pronoun "mine", not "my".

g4.label: 4. She hurt ___ at football practice.
g4.why: She is both the person who hurts and the person who is hurt, so use the reflexive "herself".

g5.label: 5. Tom lost his phone, so I lent him ___.
g5.why: "Lent him mine" means "lent him my phone". With no noun after the gap, use the possessive pronoun "mine".

g6.label: 6. We built the tree house ___.
g6.why: We built it with our own hands, so the reflexive "ourselves" fits. "Ours" means "belonging to us".

g7.label: 7. The house on the corner is ___.
g7.why: There is no noun after the gap, so use the possessive pronoun "theirs" (= belonging to them). "Their" needs a noun.

g8.label: 8. The dog hurt ___ leg yesterday.
g8.why: "Leg" follows the gap, and the leg belongs to the dog. "Its" has no apostrophe when it shows ownership; "it's" means "it is".
